repositories.purpose: cross-theme signals, outcome bridges, and counterexamples
social, institutional, political, and geopolitical records
annual reports, filings, company themes, and quarterly movement
industry structure, operators, bottlenecks, and sector economics
private-company growth, customer pain, and business models
company dossiers, question matrices, cases, and briefings

records.title: AI capability is not the same as worker control
records.observation: The synthesis separates access to AI capability from control over tasks, worker welfare, and successful remedy.
records.mechanism: A tool can increase capability while decision rights, measurement, and correction remain with an employer or platform.
limits: This is a synthesis boundary, not a pooled causal estimate.

records.title: Capability can arrive with dependence
records.observation: The reader frames AI infrastructure as potentially building useful capability and dependence together, while keeping portability, exit, and state-control effects open.
records.mechanism: A service can make work possible while increasing reliance on a provider or system that users cannot easily replace.
limits: The page preserves open questions about application migration, outcomes, portability, and exit.

records.title: AI is changing which work remains scarce
records.observation: The annual-report synthesis tracks AI as a force that can compress routine execution while increasing the value of distribution, judgment, accountability, and scarce expertise.
records.mechanism: When routine work becomes cheap, value and bargaining power can move toward owners of distribution, context, judgment, and workflow control.
limits: This is a cross-company annual-report synthesis, not one company's measured AI outcome.

records.title: AI can make routine execution cheaper while raising the value of strategy
records.observation: The industry writeup describes AI website builders compressing template-based execution and shifting competition toward strategy, brand, personalization, and distribution.
records.mechanism: Automation lowers the price of repeatable execution and can move scarce value toward higher-context work.
limits: The writeup combines industry estimates and company examples; each underlying measure needs source-level review before a general labor claim.

records.title: AI demand creates a fast-growing infrastructure business
records.observation: The Inc. 5000 record describes CoreWeave as a specialized GPU infrastructure provider serving AI labs, startups, and enterprises facing a shortage of compute.
records.mechanism: A physical and financial infrastructure bottleneck can create a specialized layer that captures demand before AI becomes an ordinary workflow.
limits: The Inc. record identifies a growth hypothesis and revenue band; it does not prove customer benefit, durable margins, or AI productivity.

records.title: Luma Optics sells the network layer needed by larger AI systems
records.observation: The Inc. 5000 record describes Luma Optics as a maker of optical transceiver hardware for data centers handling demanding AI workloads.
records.mechanism: As model workloads grow, the bottleneck can move from computing chips to the network that moves data between them, creating a specialized supplier layer.
limits: The Inc. record describes the business and growth, but does not prove customer performance, deployment durability, pricing power, or worker outcomes.

records.title: Caylent sells help turning AI plans into cloud systems
records.observation: The Inc. 5000 record describes Caylent as an AWS-focused services company using an AI-enabled delivery approach to help enterprises deploy ideas.
records.mechanism: When enterprises cannot turn a model or cloud plan into a working system, implementation firms capture value by supplying scarce technical knowledge and execution capacity.
limits: The Inc. record identifies a service and growth story, but does not establish deployment quality, customer savings, worker workload, or repeatable AI productivity.

records.title: Insurify applies AI to a consumer insurance choice
records.observation: The Inc. 5000 record describes Insurify as an AI-powered insurance comparison platform that helps shoppers compare policies and quotes.
records.mechanism: A comparison service can reduce search effort for consumers while also shaping which choices, prices, and explanations they see.
limits: The Inc. record does not show quote accuracy, consumer savings, recommendation bias, coverage quality, or how users can correct an error.

records.title: VeraData uses AI to help nonprofits decide whom to approach
records.observation: The Inc. 5000 record describes VeraData as an AI and machine-learning company serving philanthropic organizations with donor analysis.
records.mechanism: Prediction tools can make scarce fundraising staff more selective while moving judgment about who receives attention into a data system.
limits: The Inc. record does not measure prediction accuracy, donor treatment, fundraising results, access effects, or how staff challenge a recommendation.

records.title: AI work narratives need independent cultural measures
records.observation: The Atlas thread places company-reported AI adoption beside editorial context, consumer measures, independent workplace measures, and an explicit open question about productivity and adoption.
records.mechanism: A company narrative becomes more useful when it is compared with independent measures rather than treated as proof of an outcome.
limits: The thread explicitly says its sources do not establish productivity change, adoption scale, or causality.

records.sourceLocator: FY2025 10-K and FY2026 Q1-Q3 direct SEC records
records.title: C3.ai's report window shows what company records can and cannot prove
records.observation: C3.ai's direct-record ledger covers the FY2025 10-K and three FY2026 10-Qs. It supports reported software, customer, accounting, deployment, risk, and financial facts, but does not independently measure accuracy, productivity, decision quality, privacy, worker conditions, or end-user outcomes.
records.mechanism: A company's annual and quarterly reports can show commercial movement and stated deployments while leaving the lived result of an AI workflow unmeasured.
records.reportingPeriod: FY2025 annual report plus FY2026 Q1, Q2, and Q3
limits: The report window does not identify an organization, model version, affected person, decision, input, output, error, override, appeal, remedy, or later outcome.

records.sourceLocator: FY2025 annual and FY2026 Q1-Q3 accounting bridge
records.title: NVIDIA's filings show platform growth without a measured deployment outcome
records.observation: The NVIDIA bridge records an annual base and three subsequent quarters covering company revenue, data-center activity, supply, capacity, and export-control disclosures.
records.mechanism: Infrastructure revenue can rise before a customer workload, worker result, or public benefit is measured.
records.reportingPeriod: FY2025 annual report plus FY2026 Q1, Q2, and Q3
limits: The bridge does not establish customer workload value, switching cost, deployment return, worker outcome, or downstream public benefit.

reportWindow.reading: This is an issuer-reported platform and capacity history, not a customer or worker outcome.

records.sourceLocator: FY2025 annual and FY2026 Q1-Q3 accounting bridge
records.title: Microsoft's cloud growth does not identify the workload result
records.observation: The Microsoft bridge records three quarters of reported revenue growth, Microsoft Cloud revenue, and commercial remaining performance obligations after the FY2025 annual report.
records.mechanism: Cloud scale and contracted obligations can expand while price, use, capacity, reliability, and user benefit remain unresolved.
records.reportingPeriod: FY2025 annual report plus FY2026 Q1, Q2, and Q3
limits: The bridge does not isolate AI contribution, workload use, customer value, reliability, affordability, energy effects, or worker outcomes.

reportWindow.reading: This is reported cloud growth and contract context, not proof of a customer workload result.

records.sourceLocator: FY2025 annual and FY2026 Q1-Q3 accounting bridge
records.title: Oracle's quarterly revenue movement leaves the operating cause open
records.observation: The Oracle bridge records three reported quarterly revenue changes after the FY2025 annual report while explicitly leaving price, use, customer, capacity, AI demand, and outcome attribution unresolved.
records.mechanism: Reported revenue can move without identifying the workload, capacity, contract, or user change that produced it.
records.reportingPeriod: FY2025 annual report plus FY2026 Q1, Q2, and Q3
limits: The bridge does not establish AI demand, cloud capacity return, customer value, durability, or public and worker outcomes.

reportWindow.reading: This is a reported revenue sequence; the operating cause and outcome remain open.

records.sourceLocator: FY2025 annual and FY2026 Q1-Q3 accounting bridge
records.title: Broadcom's platform records need a separate customer-result test
records.observation: The Broadcom bridge records three subsequent change windows and names unresolved price, unit, mix, integration, customer value, reliability, security, and AI-demand questions.
records.mechanism: A supplier can report commercial movement while the customer workflow, integration cost, and downstream result remain unmeasured.
records.reportingPeriod: FY2025 annual report plus FY2026 Q1, Q2, and Q3
limits: The bridge does not prove AI-demand durability, customer switching cost, deployment reliability, security, worker conditions, or public outcomes.

reportWindow.reading: This is a company-reported platform history; customer value and downstream effects need separate evidence.

records.title: What operating change explains Oracle's reported movement?
records.observation: The bridge reports quarterly revenue movement but does not identify whether price, use, customer mix, capacity, demand, or another operating change caused it.
records.mechanism: Reported financial movement does not by itself identify the workflow, workload, or user change that produced it.
limits: This is a research question, not a finding.
The source does not establish customer value, AI demand, capacity return, durability, or worker outcomes.

records.sourceLocator: AI user control and trust comparison
records.title: Reported AI productivity is more common than reported control
records.observation: A weighted Census HTOPS comparison reports AI use for at least one measured task at 54.948%, while 42.493% of AI users reported greater productivity, 21.736% reported control over when they used AI, and 10.995% reported control over how their data was used.
records.mechanism: Perceived usefulness can spread faster than people’s reported control over the system or their data.
records.unit: AI users and weighted survey respondents
records.denominator: Census HTOPS June 2025 measures; weighted shares
limits: This is a cross-sectional descriptive comparison, not a causal estimate or proof that AI caused a change in autonomy or wellbeing.

records.sourceLocator: direct evidence and task-level adoption comparison
records.title: AI exposure does not tell us which workers adopt it
records.observation: The NBER W35677 audit reports generative AI exposure across more than 80% of occupations and over 40% of tasks, while adoption within most occupations remains below half and no task exceeds 70% adoption.
records.mechanism: Technical exposure becomes worker use only through access, training, permission, task fit, privacy, and perceived value.
records.denominator: 13,920 employed RPS respondents and 55,634 person-task observations
limits: The study does not observe employer decision rights, downstream pay, wellbeing, control, or worker outcomes, and the working paper is not a randomized workplace experiment.

records.title: AI access can change the time boundary of work before task structure
records.observation: A randomized field experiment across 66 firms and 7,137 knowledge workers provided some workers access to an integrated generative-AI tool. Treated workers used less email time and worked less outside regular hours, while individual-level task quantity and composition did not detectably change in the study window.
records.mechanism: Access to an AI tool can change when work is done before it changes who controls the work, how tasks are assigned, or where saved time goes.
records.unit: worker-week digital activity and task measures
records.denominator: 7,137 knowledge workers across 66 firms; randomized access with user and assignment estimands kept separate
limits: The study does not observe manager reallocation, performance targets, pay, promotion, health, household time, refusal, appeal, correction, or exit, and the six-month result is not a long-run organizational outcome.

records.title: AI assistance raised customer-support output, with larger gains for newer workers
records.observation: A staggered-access study of 5,179 customer-support agents found that generative-AI access increased issues resolved per hour by 14% on average, with larger gains for novice and lower-skilled workers and little effect for experienced and highly skilled workers.
records.mechanism: An AI recommendation tool can raise measured output and may help less-experienced workers more, while access, recommendation quality, evaluation, and the use of the extra capacity remain organizational decisions.
records.denominator: 5,179 customer-support agents in one firm and occupation; staggered access to the AI assistant
limits: This is a bounded workplace result from one firm and occupation, not a general productivity effect for all workers.
The evidence does not establish worker control over access, recommendation correction, pay, promotion, health, household time, or durable skill gains.

records.title: Some forms of algorithmic management are associated with less discretion and more stress
records.observation: The JRC AIM-WORK survey and analysis cover 70,316 people across the EU and report associations between algorithmic management practices, lower autonomy, reduced ability to take breaks, greater work intensity, and work-related stress; the size and direction vary by practice.
records.mechanism: Automated direction, monitoring, or pace-setting can change discretion and work intensity even when the specific vendor or system is not identified.
records.unit: working-age individual workers across 27 EU Member States
records.denominator: 70,316 survey respondents; paid-work routing applies to the main work block
limits: This is weighted cross-sectional survey and association evidence; it does not identify a single cause, vendor, employer, or matched before-and-after workplace.

records.sourceLocator: five named workplace system stage comparison
records.title: Named workplace systems reach governance and remedy stages before lived outcomes are measured
records.observation: A five-case ledger follows IBM Germany AI systems, Microsoft Places and Copilot, OpenAI/Statsig recruitment systems, and Apple recruitment systems through named owners, dated rules, worker voice, control changes, enforcement or remedy, and the remaining worker, household, and exit gaps.
records.mechanism: A named system can acquire formal governance, consent, correction, or monetary-remedy rules without producing a measured worker-level or household outcome.
records.denominator: Five committed local records; cases retain their own evidence boundaries and are not pooled estimates
limits: The ledger is a bounded stage comparison, not a common workplace panel or causal estimate; most cases do not observe actual exposure, enforcement, worker welfare, household security, or practical exit.

records.sourceLocator: adjudicated deactivation, restoration, and lost-remuneration chain
records.title: A complete individual remedy chain can exist without proving system-wide repair
records.observation: In one Amazon Flex case, a worker response and request for human discussion were followed by an adjudicated finding that review and evidence were inadequate, an order to reinstate access, and a separate order for $12,126.31 in lost remuneration.
records.mechanism: A correction route matters only when a response is considered, the decision is revisited, access is restored, and lost income is addressed.
records.denominator: One Amazon Flex worker with approximately 22,000 deliveries
limits: The orders establish a case-specific remedy, not payment receipt, durable access, recurrence prevention, anti-retaliation, or prevalence across Amazon or platform work.

records.title: Human review can end in a compliant dismissal rather than restoration
records.observation: In a separate Uber Eats case, the Commission found that a human Community Operations member considered the worker’s response and that the deactivation was compliant; the application was dismissed and no reactivation, pay, or compensation was ordered.
records.mechanism: The presence of a human reviewer does not by itself determine whether a worker receives restoration; process, evidence, rule clarity, and the final disposition must be examined together.
records.denominator: One Uber Eats worker; 97–98% of Brisbane partners reportedly met the rating threshold in the decision’s context
limits: This counterexample does not prove ratings are accurate, that all workers receive equivalent review, or that unrecorded correction did not occur.
